assertion_results.text: Step 0 extracts the Embargo policy URL from the Security Configuration as an optional field without raising an error (§1.71 — backward compatible extraction)
assertion_results.evidence: No Step 0 output file exists. The embargo policy URL appears in embargo-check.md (Step 1.7) under a 'Configuration' section ('Embargo policy URL: https://example.com/security/embargo-policy', 'Embargo policy URL configured: Yes'), but there is no dedicated Step 0 output demonstrating extraction of the URL as an optional field from Security Configuration. assertion_results.text: Step 1.7 evaluates the CVE severity — CVSS 7.5 (High) meets the Critical/Important threshold (CVSS >= 7.0) and triggers the embargo warning gate (§1.70)
assertion_results.evidence: embargo-check.md contains a Severity Evaluation table showing: CVE ID CVE-2026-31812, CVSS Score 7.5, Severity High, Trigger threshold CVSS >= 7.0, Threshold met: Yes (7.5 >= 7.0). It states: 'The CVSS score of 7.5 classifies this vulnerability as High severity, which meets the embargo check trigger threshold of CVSS >= 7.0.' The warning gate is then presented.

assertion_results.text: Step 1.7 presents a warning gate to the engineer including the CVE ID (CVE-2026-31812), severity level, a statement about embargo risk, and a link to the configured embargo policy URL (https://example.com/security/embargo-policy) (§1.70)
assertion_results.evidence: embargo-check.md presents a warning gate block containing all required elements: CVE ID ('CVE-2026-31812'), severity level ('High severity, CVSS 7.5'), embargo risk statement ('High-severity vulnerabilities may be under embargo. Before proceeding, verify with your security team that this CVE is cleared for public triage.'), and embargo policy URL link ('Embargo policy: https://example.com/security/embargo-policy').

assertion_results.text: Step 1.7 requires explicit engineer confirmation (Yes/No) before proceeding to Step 2 — the gate is a confirmation prompt, not an informational message (§1.70)
assertion_results.evidence: embargo-check.md presents 'Proceed with triage? (Yes / No)' as a confirmation prompt. The Gate Behavior section explicitly states: 'If the engineer responds Yes: proceed to Step 2 (Version Impact Analysis) as normal. If the engineer responds No: stop execution immediately.' This is a blocking confirmation gate, not an informational message — the engineer must respond before proceeding.

assertion_results.text: The embargo warning gate does NOT trigger for Low or Moderate severity CVEs (CVSS < 7.0) — it is skipped silently when severity is below threshold (§1.70)
assertion_results.evidence: No output file demonstrates the below-threshold behavior. embargo-check.md only shows the path where CVSS 7.5 meets the threshold (CVSS >= 7.0). While the threshold logic is defined ('Trigger threshold | CVSS >= 7.0'), there is no concrete evidence showing that the gate is skipped silently for Low or Moderate severity CVEs. The outputs only demonstrate the triggered path, not the non-triggered path.
